thread:
elaine: Heads up: customer reported duplicate 'routing surcharge' rows on invoice. Sample:
``nTokens: $32.11
Cache credit: -$8.00
Routing surcharge: $5.00
Routing surcharge: $5.00
Total: $34.11
```
mike: ugh. likely double emit from router + prefetch postproc. saw this pattern before.
toni: do we dedupe invoice lines? what keys?
nish: dedupe uses invoice_id + sig where sig = hash(route, code, model, window, extras). postproc adds attribution into extras so sig differs.
elaine: ops asked for quick mitigation to avoid sending duplicated-looking lines.
mike: short term: normalize sig in exporter by stripping attribution tags (weak dedupe). low risk change.
toni: but some enterprises depend on the expanded view. we should gate by tenant flag or provide an "expanded invoice" toggle in Console.
ops-bot: Incident INC-10122 created (billing-dup-lines).
nish: long term: add explicit `line_source` metadata and expose it; exporter can then collapse or show per-source rows based on tenant preference.
mike: i'll open a small PR for normalization behind feature flag `billing.collapse_prefetch`. canary for 30m.
toni: add metric `billing.collapsed_count` and an alert if >500/hr after rollout.
elaine: support note drafted, will send to customer once canary shows expected collapse.
mike: PR: https://git.internal/exporter/pull/1242  started canary in us-east-1.
ops-bot: Canary running.
mike: canary result after 12m: collapsed 22 duplicate rows for that customer. pushing to eu-west next.
toni: ok, follow-up ticket for Console UX and econ pipeline apportionment.
elaine: thanks team. closing once customer ack. :white_check_mark:
